- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish or stagnant sentiment.
- Model consistently over-estimates early in the 30-day horizon (especially days 1–5) when sentiment is mixed or neutral — apply downward bias to first 5 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ above 60), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days — cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use sentiment to trigger early correction.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model tends to ignore it — apply slight upward bias to counteract over-optimism.
- Sentiment volatility (rapid swings) correlates with model lag — if sentiment shifts sharply, delay forecast adjustment until 2–3 days later to avoid overreaction.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price range in high-sentiment periods — add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.75 over last 5 days.
